neighbours.label: The word right after 'further' used as a verb, 'to further X's cause / ends / career' ("to further⟦ their⟧ own ends", "further⟦ing⟧"); weaker on the verb 'advance'; silent on adverb or adjective 'further'
fire: The senator used the hearings mainly to further his own ambitions.
The society was set up to further the study of local history.
Both parties accused each other of using the crisis to further their own agendas.
She moved to Vienna in order to further her training as a singer.
The grant is meant to further the cause of rural education.
Critics said the merger did little except to further the interests of shareholders.
He wrote the pamphlet to further his campaign against the tax.
The alliance helped each country to further its own aims in the region.
quiet: The senator walked a little further along the corridor before answering.
For further details about local history, write to the society.
Both parties sat even further apart after the crisis.
She moved to Vienna and never looked further than the opera house.
The grant is meant to pay for books in rural schools.
Critics said the merger did little except raise prices for customers.
He wrote nothing further about his campaign against the tax.
The border lies further north than most maps of the region show.

notes: Card: peaks ' the', 'ing', ' their', 'ed' all right after verbal 'further', and ' advance' x4. Probes: 'to further his own career' 0.89, 'to further the cause' 0.78, 'advance their interests' 0.46; 'further down the valley' 0.01, 'For further information' 0.01, 'promote her own career' 0.22.
